fixes.explanation: Yes, baker! The proverb says, “Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.” Discipline is what it names as driving foolishness far away. That's the answer the verse gives. I'm a grown stamper and I still need a little of that now and then.

Not quite, friend. The proverb says the simple “…keep going and suffer the consequences.” Suffering the consequences is the opposite of coming through without a scratch. The prudent are the ones who see danger and take cover.

Yes, “he who guards his soul stays far from them.” He doesn't test how thorny the thorns are. He just keeps his distance. Smart man. I keep my distance from a hot oven door, and my mustache thanks me.
Yes, “He who sows injustice will reap disaster…” What gets planted decides what grows. If I plant a flour sack in my kitchen, I don't harvest a bakery. The farming picture makes it easy to see.
Yes, “Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart…” The verse goes on: “even quarreling and insults will cease.” One mocker out the door and the whole room breathes again.

It's actually true, friend. The proverb says “He who loves a pure heart and gracious lips will have the king for a friend.” That's exactly what the verse says about him. The king as his friend is the promise.

Yes, the slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!” Now that's a dramatic line. I think I'd have to sit down after saying that one. The verse calls the man who says it the slacker.
A storm is a decent excuse, friend, but it's not his. The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!” A lion, right outside. That's the line the verse gives.

Yes, “Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty.” Squeeze the poor to get rich, or give gifts to the rich, and the verse says either one leads to the same place. Both roads end in poverty. The ending doesn't change.
Power is a fair guess, friend, but the proverb says otherwise. Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich “…will surely lead to poverty.” The word the verse gives is poverty.
